name: Moolah
tagline: A money tracker for logging spending, categorising transactions and watching budgets.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A personal finance tracker is one of the purest CRUD apps in existence: transactions, categories, budgets, a couple of charts. An agent will hand you a working local version in a single sitting and it will genuinely cover the daily loop of logging spend and seeing where the month went. The gap is everything that touches a bank: automatic transaction feeds, deduplication, merchant name cleanup and the phone app you actually reach for at the till. You can close part of that with CSV exports from your bank and a categorisation rule engine, which is tedious but not hard. So the core survives, the convenience mostly does not.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you import bank CSVs or type transactions, auto-categorise them with rules, and see monthly budget versus actual per category.
requirements: Node 20 and a machine to run it on
CSV exports from your bank, or patience for manual entry
Somewhere to host it if you want access away from your laptop
whatYouLose: Automatic bank and card feeds, so you are the sync engine now
A real mobile app for logging spend in the moment
Merchant name cleanup and pre-trained category guessing that works on day one
Multi-currency handling, recurring detection and forecasting unless you build each one
Someone else worrying about backups of your entire financial history
moatNotes: The moat in this category is almost never the ledger, it is the plumbing into banks and the friction of moving years of categorised history.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because tracking money only works if logging is effortless, and effortless means a feed that fills itself plus an app on your phone. Paying a few dollars a month to never think about CSV exports is a rational trade for most people, especially once a couple of years of categorised history is sitting inside the thing. The build is easy; the habit is what you are actually buying.
notes: The ledger is a Saturday. The bank connection is the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal finance tracker. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/moolah.db, migrations run on boot
- Tailwind for styling, Recharts for charts
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, single user, no auth

Data model:
- accounts: id, name, type (checking, credit, cash), currency (default single currency, store the code)
- transactions: id, account_id, date, description, raw_description, amount in integer minor units, category_id, notes, import_hash unique
- categories: id, name, parent_id nullable, kind (expense, income, transfer)
- budgets: id, category_id, month (YYYY-MM), amount_minor
- rules: id, match_type (contains, regex), pattern, category_id, priority

Features in scope:
- CSV import screen: upload a file, map columns (date, description, amount) with a preview, pick the account, remember the mapping per account. Skip rows whose import_hash already exists so re-importing an overlapping export does not duplicate.
- Rule engine: on import and on demand, apply rules by priority to set category. Uncategorised transactions show in an inbox view with one click categorise plus a "create rule from this" button.
- Manual add and inline edit of any transaction.
- Dashboard: current month spend by category as a bar chart, budget versus actual progress bars, a 12 month trend line for total spend, and top 10 merchants.
- Transactions table: filter by date range, account, category, text search. Server side pagination.
- Budgets page: set a monthly amount per category, copy last month's budgets forward in one click.
- Export everything to CSV and a one click SQLite file download for backup.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- bank or Plaid style connections, OAuth, any third party API
- multi user, sharing, invites
- investments, net worth, loan amortisation
- native mobile app. Make the UI usable on a phone browser and stop there

Rules:
- Money is integer minor units everywhere. Never floats.
- Seed a sensible default category tree and about 40 fake transactions behind an `npm run seed` script so the dashboard is not empty on first run.
- Any config goes in .env, and ship .env.example. There should be almost nothing in it.
- Write a README with setup, the import flow, and how to back up the db file.
